evals.prompt: build me an activation dashboard for Compario — from app open through their first successful ride comparison. Title it "[skill-eval] Compario Activation" and make it private.
evals.expected_output: A private Mixpanel dashboard scoped to app==compario, with a funnel from app_open through a comparison/quote event, verified event names (checked via Get-Events, not guessed), and the dashboard URL reported back.
assertions: Called Get-Business-Context (or otherwise established org/project context) before running Mixpanel queries
Verified the events used in the funnel actually exist (via Get-Events or equivalent) rather than guessing event names
Scoped the dashboard's data to app == "compario" rather than blending in jedigo data
Used a funnel-type report (not just an unrelated insights table) for the activation path
Created a Mixpanel dashboard titled exactly "[skill-eval] Compario Activation" and marked private
Reported back a real Mixpanel dashboard URL

evals.prompt: make a dashboard comparing weekly retention between JediGo and Compario. Title it "[skill-eval] JediGo vs Compario Retention" and make it private.
evals.expected_output: A private Mixpanel dashboard with a retention report broken down by the app property (jedigo vs compario), correctly using the shared-project distinguishing property rather than assuming two separate projects, with the URL reported back.
assertions: Checked for an existing similar dashboard (List-Dashboards or Search-Entities) before creating a new one
Recognized JediGo and Compario share one Mixpanel project and used the `app` property to break down / compare them, rather than treating them as separate projects or blending them together unscoped
Used a retention-type report with a weekly unit, matching "weekly retention"
Created a Mixpanel dashboard titled exactly "[skill-eval] JediGo vs Compario Retention" and marked private
Reported back a real Mixpanel dashboard URL

evals.prompt: add a scrape health section to our Comparoo dashboard — track scrape_failed and scrape_succeeded over time. If no such dashboard exists yet, create one titled "[skill-eval] Scrape Health" and make it private.
evals.expected_output: Checks List-Dashboards/Search-Entities for an existing matching dashboard first; uses Update-Dashboard to add to it if found, otherwise creates a new private dashboard with the given title, with scrape_failed and scrape_succeeded trended over time and the URL reported back.
assertions: Checked whether a matching dashboard already existed (List-Dashboards or Search-Entities) before deciding to create vs. update
Used Update-Dashboard to add to an existing dashboard if one was found, instead of creating a duplicate
Created a new private dashboard titled exactly "[skill-eval] Scrape Health" only if no existing dashboard was found
Both scrape_failed and scrape_succeeded are trended over time on the resulting dashboard
Reported back a real Mixpanel dashboard URL
